newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: Portugal yr/yr inflation to fall significantly-INE.
newsitem.headline: Portugal yr/yr inflation to fall significantly-INE.

text.p: Portugal's year-on-year inflation will fall significantly up to July, the National Statistics Institute (INE) said in its latest commentary on the Portuguese economy.
It also said that non-tradable goods prices rose 4.5 percent year-on-year in March, down from 4.8 percent in February.
Referring to the economy as a whole, INE said that growth was lively over the first quarter of the year, helped by the positive trend in internal demand.
Purchasing power rose, exports were continuing to rise and unemployment fell in this period, it said.

INE said that "a significant fall in the year-on-year variation in the consumer price index (CPI) was expected until the end of July, given that the 1996 period was marked by unusual rises in prices for some food products."

Analysts have forecast that Portugal's year-on-year inflation, which dropped to 2.5 percent in March from 2.9 percent in February, will fall further as meat price rises triggered by last year's mad cow disease scare drop out of the index.
INE said that factory-gate prices, excluding food and petroleum products, rose only 0.6 percent year-on-year in the first quarter.
